VBO:0200551.summary: Friendly and close to people in its breed standard, the French White and Black Hound is valued in deer hunts for a fine nose, a carrying voice and diligent trail work. Its modern type developed from Saintonge stock during the nineteenth century, with later Poitevin and Gascon Saintongeois crosses. It gained a standard in 1957.
VBO:0200551.shortDescription: A friendly French pack hound, valued in deer hunts for its fine nose, carrying voice and diligent trail work.

sources.title: FCI220 — French White and Black Hound standard
sources.evidence: Friendly close to humans and manageable in kennels; deer hunts value fine nose, diligence, seriousness and voice. Present type appeared second half19thcentury from Saintonge stock with later Poitevin/GasconSaintongeois crosses; standard1957. Square balanced largehound, long narrow slightly domed head/longer muzzle/subtle stop/blacknose/darkeyes, eye-level curled long ears reaching nose, deep rather than broad chest/slighttuck, strong flat legcourses/long lean feet, full thickroot relatively high carriedtail; short dense blackwhite mantle/speckles with pale minor tan accents, not tricolor.
